⊢.justification: The void state before factorization begins; the target integer exists but no relations or structure have been established.

⊣.justification: The terminal anchor where the product of found factors equals N, closing the system.

≻.justification: Forward morphism selecting polynomials f and g to map N into algebraic number fields, driving the system toward relation generation.

≺.justification: Reverse morphism descending from the algebraic relation back to the integer domain to extract a non-trivial factor via GCD.

⋈.justification: Composition chaining individual smooth relations into the large sparse matrix required for linear algebra.

⊙.justification: Identity self-reference; the set of primes defining the smoothness threshold remains invariant throughout the sieving process.

∈.justification: Co-multiplication splitting the search space into the rational side (f) and algebraic side (g) of the number field.

∋.justification: Multiplication rejoining the rational and algebraic dependencies into a single linear dependency vector over GF(2).

⊤.justification: Affirmative state where a candidate number factors completely over the factor base.

⊥.justification: Negative state where a candidate contains a prime factor outside the factor base.

⊞.justification: Holding both the rational and algebraic smoothness simultaneously without immediate reduction, maintaining the tension required for the square.

⊡.justification: Permanent, append-only record of a valid relation (a, b) added to the matrix.

phase_3.void_description: No relations collected; the matrix is empty.
phase_3.true_description: A valid relation is found and added to the matrix.
phase_3.false_description: A candidate fails smoothness; no relation is recorded.
phase_3.both_description: A candidate is smooth on both sides simultaneously, creating a valid relation that holds both algebraic and rational properties.

steps.domain_action: Initialize the system with the target integer N to be factored.
Define the Factor Base, the set of small primes for smoothness testing.
Select polynomials f and g to map N into two distinct algebraic number fields.
Branch the sieving process into rational and algebraic domains.
Check if the rational side of a candidate is smooth over the factor base.
Check if the algebraic side of a candidate is smooth over the factor base.
Hold the candidate in a paradice state where both rational and algebraic smoothness are simultaneously verified.
Record the valid relation (a, b) into the permanent relation log.
Aggregate the recorded relations into a large sparse matrix over GF(2).
Branch the linear algebra phase into finding the kernel of the matrix.
Identify a subset of relations whose product forms a square on the rational side.
Identify a subset of relations whose product forms a square on the algebraic side.
Rejoin the rational and algebraic square roots into a single dependency vector.
Compute the GCD of the difference between the square roots and N to extract a factor.
Verify the factor divides N, closing the factorization process.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational work to test smoothness and solve the linear system
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Integer N with no known factors
phase_6.post_cycle_state: Integer N decomposed into factors p and q
